chunks: From the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:

Whoever swears by Allah, let him be truthful; and whoever is sworn to by Allah, let him be pleased (with it); and whoever is not pleased is not from Allah in any way. As for when he denies the property and does not make him swear an oath upon it, then property comes to him at his hand, it is permissible for him to take from it according to the amount of his property after he says the words we mentioned. And whenever he has property and the denier denies it, then the denier deposits with him a property, it is disliked for him to take from it because this follows the manner of treachery, and treachery is not permissible for him in any state.

key_terms.اِسْتَوْدَعَهُ: he deposited with him (as a trust)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping disputed property when the claimant denies ownership but does not swear an oath?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this narration to distinguish between the spiritual etiquette of oaths and the jurisprudential mechanics of property retention (*qabd*). The text highlights a critical legal nuance: while denying ownership without an oath allows the possessor to retain a proportional amount, accepting a subsequent deposit transforms the relationship into a trust (*amanah*), making retention akin to treachery (*khiyanah*). This underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the integrity of the trust relationship over mere possession.
